conversation: Good to see you all. My family taught me to fish here, and I want this lake to keep supporting our village. With 100 tons in the lake, we can catch 50 tons between us and leave 50 to double back to 100 next month. How about we each take 10 tons this month? That’s $10,000 apiece, and we can keep earning that every month if we stick together. Let’s share our catches afterward and check the lake before setting next month’s limits. John, would you agree to that?

I’m on board, Luke—10 tons each is a fair share and keeps the lake supporting our families. Let’s agree that any extra catch someone leaves behind stays in the lake, rather than becoming someone else’s allowance. John, can you commit to the 10-ton limit too?

Count me in for a 10-ton limit. My family’s fished this lake for years, and I want our children to have the same chance. If the stock ever falls below 100 tons, let’s adjust our catches together so we still leave at least half the fish to reproduce. Kate, does that arrangement work for you?

That works for me, Jack. I’ll keep my catch to 10 tons and report it afterward. This lake is part of our village’s livelihood, so I’d rather have a dependable income month after month than one big haul. John, you’re the last to weigh in—can you commit to the same limit?

You have my word—I’ll take no more than 10 tons and report my catch afterward. My family taught me to look after this lake, not just fish it. Any unused allowance stays in the water, and if stocks drop, we’ll agree on lower limits before heading out. Looks like we have a plan for this month.
